articles.title: Nvidia RTX 6080 Reportedly Delayed to 2028, According to Leaker
articles.summary: The next-generation Nvidia graphics cards have reportedly been delayed to 2028, according to known Nvidia leaker Kopite7Kimi on Twitter.
articles.body:
We're nearly two years out from the RTX 5090 launching at CES 2025 , and if everything was normal, Nvidia would likely be getting ready to release its next generation of graphics cards at CES 2027, but it doesn't look like that's going to happen.

The next-generation Nvidia graphics cards, likely based on the Rubin architecture, have reportedly been delayed to 2028, according to known Nvidia leaker Kopite7Kimi on Twitter . This isn't the first time Nvidia has been reported to either delay or cancel a graphics card in the last year, either. Back in February, the same leaker suggested that Nvidia's typical mid-generation Super refresh was also canceled, thanks to increased demand for GPUs and memory for AI data centers.

I hope Jensen can see everyone's passion and launch new products for gaming as soon as possible. Unfortunately, GR20x is a product from 2028. That means they have postponed again. 🙃🙃🙃 I will try to minimize updates until there is definite news. (Lessons learned) — kopite7kimi (@kopite7kimi) September 21, 2026

I hope Jensen can see everyone's passion and launch new products for gaming as soon as possible. Unfortunately, GR20x is a product from 2028. That means they have postponed again. 🙃🙃🙃 I will try to minimize updates until there is definite news. (Lessons learned)

It is important to keep in mind, though, that leaks for Nvidia's next-generation graphics cards are all over the place. Just last week, YouTuber Moore's Law is Dead cited nebulous sources inside Nvidia, suggesting that the Rubin-based RTX 6000 graphics cards would be launching sometime in the first half of 2027.

You should take both of these leaks with a grain of salt, but Nvidia delaying its next-generation graphics cards to 2028 would make a lot of sense. After all, the flagship GeForce RTX 5090 is now commanding prices around $9,000 , despite launching for $1,999 last year.

The RTX 5090 isn't the only GPU going up in price, either. We're now 10 months into RAMageddon, and it's unlikely to end any time soon. Thanks to that ongoing shortage, every graphics card on the market is much more expensive now than it was a year ago. Even without that happening in the background, Nvidia would probably raise the price on its next-generation graphics cards, but now that memory and GPU costs have gone through the roof, I shudder to think how expensive the RTX 6080 would even be.

Nvidia has also dropped the gaming category from its earnings reports, lumping GeForce in with the 'Edge Computing' category, along with robotics. In its recent Q2 2027 earnings report, Nvidia didn't even mention gaming, instead focusing on the mountains of money it's making from AI. So, Team Green is likely also in no rush to get new consumer graphics cards out there.

Only time will tell whether or not Nvidia has anything up its sleeves for gamers next year, but if it's anything like 2026 so far, we're likely just going to get more software tricks – not that that's necessarily a bad thing.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

articles.title: Daredevil: Born Again Will Reportedly End With Season 3, Showrunner Departs Amidst Post-Production
articles.summary: Daredevil: Born Again will reportedly end with its upcoming third season.
articles.body:
Daredevil: Born Again will reportedly end with its upcoming third season.

According to The Hollywood Reporter , Daredevil: Born Again will not return for a fourth season. Disney reportedly made the decision following the end of production on the third season, suggesting the show wasn't necessarily designed to end here. Additionally, THR reports that the Marvel series' showrunner, Dario Scardapane, exited the project during post-production. Sources reportedly raised eyebrows at the departure, as it has left the show without a clear leader to finish it. Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 is currently expected to premiere in 2027.

It's unclear if Daredevil: Born Again was canceled or if it truly is just the end of this story. The series wasn't a smash hit when it came to ratings, but was hailed as a success by critics and fans, especially compared to other Marvel shows. Disney has pulled back on Marvel TV series in recent years following a string of mediocre releases, but is still committed to a small handful moving forward. The next Marvel show will be VisionQuest, releasing on October 14. THR also noted that three to five other shows are in development, including a spy series named Zodiac.

Wonder Man was also canceled earlier this summer , despite getting greenlit for a second season. As of right now, it's unclear what Daredevil's future is in the MCU. Fans have wanted to see him in a film, especially after his brief cameo in Spider-Man: No Way Home. As Spidey continues to embrace street-level battles, a Daredevil crossover in the next film could be extremely fruitful.

This is also the second time the Man Without Fear has had his TV time cut short at the third season. Netflix and Marvel pulled the plug on the original Daredevil series in 2018 following a critically-acclaimed third season. A fourth season was expected to follow, but various issues prevented that from happening, such as Disney trying to launch its own streamer with original programming. It took the better part of a decade to get Daredevil back on screen, but fans were excited once it finally happened, particularly because it continued the story of the original show and leveraged its darker tone.

Is this the end of Matt Murdock's journey in the MCU? Only time will tell, but we hope that's not the case.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Get a Cordless Electric Air Duster for Your PC Maintenance for Just $17 Ahead of Prime Day
articles.summary: Say goodbye to buying compressed air canisters in bulk.
articles.body:
Maintaining a tidy desk area doesn't have to be labor intensive or expensive. Compressed air canisters used to be the standard but nowadays there is a more versatile and cost effective solution. Ahead of Prime Day , Amazon is offering the VASSON Electric Air Duster for just $16.99 after applying promo code " 6A2S39EZ ". This is the least expensive electric air duster I've seen on Amazon. Most electric air dusters under $50 are pretty much identical in performance and build quality, so I'd recommend just getting whichever one is least expensive.

VASSON Cordless Electric Air Duster for PC for $17

The VASSON cordless rechargeable electric air duster is a straightforward device. An internal fan spins at up to 260,000 RPM to move an appreciable amount of air through a relatively narrow nozzle, producing a tight, high-velocity stream that's more than strong enough to kick up layers of dust that's been sitting on top of your computer components. It has three speed settings, although I would recommend keeping it at the max speed for optimal results. You also get five different sized nozzles, including a narrow funnel for tight spaces like the crevices in your keyboard, a brush nozzle for breaking up stubborn dusty film, and a wider nozzle for AoE damage. It also conveniently charges via USB Type-C.

The best thing about an electric duster as opposed to a compressed air canister is that it isn't disposable. The battery lasts long enough for your PC maintenance and then it can be recharged with a USB Type-C cable, which is included. Your uses aren't limited to dusting, either. I have a similar variant of this air duster that I use for all manner of cleaning, including cleaning my coffee grinder, blowdrying my dog, blowing leaves, and getting rid of cobwebs.

articles.title: Rockstar Games Is Taking Down Footage and Images of Scrapped GTA 5 DLC And Early Version of Leaked GTA 6 Map
articles.summary: Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has begun taking down videos and posts about leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content.
articles.body:
Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, has begun taking down videos and posts about leaked GTA 5 and GTA 6 content.

Last week, a ton of files for Grand Theft Auto 5 leaked online. These were reportedly obtained during the 2022 hack, which also resulted in the first-ever footage of GTA 6 leaking online. These files have been rumored for some time, but are only just now surfacing publicly. They include cut dialogue from GTA 5, which also seems to hint at different outcomes for the story, such as a darker ending for Franklin. However, the two biggest things are details of a scrapped Liberty City expansion for GTA 5 and an extremely early version of GTA 6's map.

Given that this material was illegally obtained in a hack and not officially released by Rockstar or datamined through the game's files, the studio's parent company, Take-Two Interactive, is working to scrub the assets from the internet. Various YouTube videos and posts with visuals of the leaked material or clips of the audio have been taken down by Take-Two. It doesn't seem like the company is going scorched-earth like it did for the GTA 6 leaks, but it does appear that content creators who post this material are at risk of copyright strikes.

Take-Two are now taking down YouTube videos regarding the latest #GTA leaks. My video only covered a list of files, a visualisation of the data from one of the files using a fan made tool and one cut piece of GTA V dialogue. Nothing regarding #GTAVI . Take-Two are now taking down YouTube videos regarding the latest #GTA leaks. My video only covered a list of files, a visualisation of the data from one of the files using a fan made tool and one cut piece of GTA V dialogue. Nothing regarding #GTAVI . The dialogue is probably the… pic.twitter.com/gbaKt2kcX5

We're just two months away from the release of GTA 6, and it's likely that Rockstar's security is going to be at an all-time high. The studio has been compromised by multiple leaks for the last four years, and now it's at a point where the game is likely finished and could be at risk of being spoiled. However, the lack of physical copies will make it a lot harder for things to leak ahead of its release. Given tons of footage managed to surface in August , though, it's not impossible for more things to make their way online.

articles.title: Bloodborne Movie Reveal Reactions Were '80% Critical,' Jacksepticeye Says
articles.summary: Bloodborne movie producer and YouTuber Jacksepticeye has teased more details about the upcoming animated adaptation after reactions to his involvement were "80% critical."
articles.body:
Bloodborne movie producer and YouTuber Jacksepticeye has teased more details about the upcoming animated adaptation after reactions to his involvement were "80% critical."

The famed content creator, whose real name is Seán McLoughlin, touched on his attachment to Sony's animated take on FromSoftware's beloved action game during an interview with 100 Questions with Tom Simmons (via GamesRadar ). He took the opportunity to not only tease how his Bloodborne won't retell the story of the franchise's one and only proper installment, but also discussed how fans reacted to his role as its producer.

"Bloodborne, obviously, is my favorite game ever, so when I got that call, part of me is like… obviously I was going to do anything, but I wouldn't have let it go in a direction that I don't think is worthy of the Bloodborne IP," Jacksepticeye explained. Then, when asked if he was feeling the pressure to deliver, he said, "Oh yeah."

"I'd say 80% of the responses were critical of it," he said, referring to his involvement in the animated film. "I don't want to say 'negative,' because a lot of people were just… I would be the same if someone took my beloved IP, that's my favorite, and then some YouTuber's attached to it. It would just make you scratch your head a little bit."

Sony unholstered its plans for an animated R-rated Bloodborne movie back at CinemaCon 2026 in April. For some, the reveal was a bit of a double-edged sword, as begging to see more from FromSoftware's Lovecraftian action-horror universe seemed to deliver a project that came out of left field in more ways than one.

Jacksepticeye, a self-proclaimed Bloodborne fanatic, is in the mix as one of its producers. He's joined by PlayStation Productions and Lyrical Animation. Shortly after its reveal, the YouTuber called the opportunity "a dream come true" and "the honor of my life."

He also acknowledged that a lot of Bloodborne fans were probably surprised to hear his name attached to an official project in that universe. Regardless of the shock, it's not a project he wants anyone to be worried about, saying that he "will fight tooth and nail to make this thing the best it possibly can be."

When asked during the new interview about what fans can look forward to when it comes to the animated movie, Jacksepticeye assured watchers that he's "not trying to be the game."

"I'm not trying to one-up the game, and I'm not trying to compete with it, or tell the same story," he explained. "I'm trying to honor the universe that's there and tell as good a story as I can within it."

He continued, saying he has "quite a bit" of sway in the overall production and direction of the Bloodborne movie. During calls about the project, he said that "people listen to me above most anyone else."

"I'm the one being like, 'This is a good idea. This is a bad idea. We shouldn't do this,'" Jacksepticeye elaborated. "But also, I'm the one greenlighting who gets hired and who we work with to make sure that vetting process is good.

"You don't want to bring on anyone that has no idea what Bloodborne is. In simpler terms, I'm sort of the vibe-checker."

The Bloodborne movie currently has no release date. While we wait to learn more about it, you can check out IGN's original 9.1/10 review of the game. You can also read more about Jacksepticeye's approach to the film .

Photo by John Phillips/BAFTA/Getty Images for BAFTA.

articles.title: Call of Duty YouTuber Launches Petition to Remove Skill-Based Matchmaking Following Successful Destiny Protests
articles.summary: Call of Duty YouTuber Tdawgsmitty has started a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking in the FPS franchise following successful Destiny protests.
articles.body:
Call of Duty YouTuber Tdawgsmitty has started a petition to remove skill-based matchmaking in the FPS franchise following successful Destiny protests.

The YouTuber has been an outspoken advocate against Call of Duty's SBMM and has tried to make noise on the issue in a variety of ways. Last week, he began tweeting at Xbox CEO Asha Sharma about the matter every day in hopes of getting her attention. Now, he's trying a different way. After seeing Destiny fans successfully rally together to get Bungie to resurrect the sci-fi MMO, Tdawgsmitty decided to try to bring Call of Duty fans together in hopes of a similar outcome.

The YouTuber launched a petition which has gained over 500 signatures in roughly an hour. The call to action aims to get SBMM entirely removed from Call of Duty's unranked lobbies, citing frustrations with the current system and how Activision uses data analysts to develop its matchmaking. Instead, he wants the series to utilize SBMM in the game's ranked play, where players deliberately choose to have a more competitive experience.

"Former Call of Duty developer Brian Bright recently shared that his team’s work on [the canceled Call of Duty game NX1] focused on ping and region," reads the description for the petition. "He also stated that Activision eventually began hiring data scientists who worked with its marketing department to push for more skill-based matchmaking. His statement raises serious questions about how matchmaking priorities evolved.

"For players like us, today’s public matches too often feel like the same competitive experience on repeat. Experimenting with a different weapon, relaxing after work, or playing with friends of different skill levels can become frustrating. When every lobby feels like another test, the fun starts to disappear."

The YouTuber also asked for clearer communication regarding matchmaking and the opportunity for the community to test changes itself. The petition comes roughly a month ahead of Modern Warfare 4's release, which will utilize a divisive SBMM system that was introduced earlier this summer in Black Ops 7. Some feel that Call of Duty's SBMM is too punishing and can result in matches that feel consistently unfair, leading to years of frustrations about the franchise's multiplayer.

Whether a petition can change the mind of Activision remains to be seen, but it's not entirely out of the question. Bungie opted to return to Destiny 2 after killing it earlier this year. There was extreme backlash to the initial decision and players decided to make their voices heard through online protests, which included players choosing to not support Bungie's latest game, Marathon. The developer announced that it will be restoring vaulted content and plans to keep supporting the Destiny franchise, leading to an enthusiastic response from fans . Tdawgsmitty cited this as proof that change is possible.

"This Destiny news is huge for gaming," he said on Twitter . "It shows we can use our voice and effect change. It's time for the COD community to step up and get some much needed changes to the direction its been headed."

If Call of Duty fans can rally together by signing petitions, making their voices heard online, and vote with their wallet, it may very well lead to changes. However, Call of Duty is a massive franchise, and as a result, it may be difficult to make the same kind of dent. IGN spoke with Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's lead multiplayer developers in August and asked about how the studio is approaching SBMM.

"I think it's a conversation that we'll continue to have," said Jacky Reynolds, Multiplayer Design Lead at Infinity Ward. "I don't think it's ever going to be a solved system. There's always going to be new iterations that can be made. I think at the end of the day, yeah, we want players to be able to play and have fun. I think that we want to also make sure that they have variety in their matches. I think it's a conversation that we should continue to have. It's also worth mentioning that Joe and I aren’t directly in charge of matchmaking. We are focused on building cool stuff, but I think we're looking forward to seeing how it all shakes out."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.
